# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** Mid-forties  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c19 P52](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0052)</sub>
- **Titles:** Miss Penrose  <sub>[v1 c19 P78](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0078)</sub>; Miss Rosalind  <sub>[v1 c19 P39](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0039)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** The princess  <sub>[v1 c19 P85](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0085)</sub>

## Appearance

Miss Rosalind is a small woman with an almost youthful face, rosy cheeks, sweet lips, large gentle wood-brown eyes with gold flecks, and dimples. She has thick, lovely, wavy snow-white hair, which she wears arranged in flattering puffs and coils. She wears delicate cream muslin dresses adorned with light-colored roses.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P44](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0044), [v1 c19 P89](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0089), [v1 c23 P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)_

## Personality

Miss Rosalind is a cheerful, lively, and imaginative woman who loves romantic fantasies, tea parties, and beautiful things. Though eccentric and prone to brooding or moods, she possesses a gentle, warm, and deeply affectionate nature, forming strong bonds with those she cares about. She is also candid, self-aware, and possesses a subtle sense of humor.

_Sources: [v1 c19 P13](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0013), [v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053), [v1 c19 P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092), [v1 c19 P97](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0097), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)_

## Traits

- Imaginative and fond of pretending  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053)</sub>
- Candid and self-aware  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c23 P7](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0007)</sub>
- Moods and brooding tendencies  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Hates being caught acting foolishly  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053)</sub>
- Proud and independent  <sub>[v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>

## Abilities

- Skilled at needlework and dressmaking  <sub>[v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016)</sub>
- Gracious host  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019), [v1 c19 P64](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0064)</sub>

## Goals

- To live comfortably and enjoy her life and imaginations despite her age  <sub>[v1 c19 P19](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0019)</sub>
- To reconnect with her former love, Stephen Stanhope  <sub>[v1 c23 P37](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0037)</sub>

## History

In her youth, Rosalind Penrose was betrothed to Stephen Stanhope. Following a misunderstanding and an argument driven by her pride, their engagement ended and Stephen departed for the United States, leaving her heartbroken. Refusing to love or marry anyone else, she lived a quiet, secluded life for twenty-five years in her sandstone home, Echo Cottage, entertaining herself with her imagination, her echoes, and a series of young maidservants whom she called 'Belinda'. She eventually met Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke when they stumbled upon her garden, forming a warm friendship with them. Nell later introduced her to Stephen's son, Cedric. Hearing of Stephen's return, Nell arranged for Stephen to visit her at Echo Cottage. The two reconciled, leading to their marriage in her garden beneath a honeysuckle arbor. Afterward, she departed with Stephen for a journey to the Pacific coast, planning to reside in Boston while keeping Echo Cottage for summer visits.

_Sources: [v1 c21 P36](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0036), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019), [v1 c23 P27](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0027), [v1 c23 P38](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0038), [v1 c25 P29](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0029), [v1 c25 P30](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0030), [v1 c29 P22](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0022), [v1 c29 P33](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0033)_

## Background by volume

- Her father named her Rosalind because he loved the scent of lavender, which he associated with her mother
- Was engaged to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago, but they separated after an argument  <sub>[v1 c21 P36](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0036), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>
- Her mother passed away ten years prior to her marriage to Stephen
- Employed a succession of young girls named Belinda to assist her in her home

## Quotes

> I was merely imagining that I was... I felt very isolated. I adore society... but hardly any individuals ever visit this place since it is extremely remote. Consequently, I simply imagined I was about to host a tea party.  <sub>[v1 c19 P53](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0053)</sub>

> A person may just as well age along with the rest of their peers... Failing to do so leaves you without a place anywhere.  <sub>[v1 c21 P22](../source/v01-c21.md#nw-v01-c21-p0022)</sub>

> I could never feel affection for anyone else, nor did I desire to. I was certain I would prefer being an unmarried woman for ten centuries over marrying anyone who was not Stephen Stanhope.  <sub>[v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>

> A fractured heart in actual life is not nearly as terrible as it appears in novels. It resembles a decayed tooth quite a bit... It suffers fits of pain and grants you an occasional restless night, but in the intervals it allows you to take pleasure in existence and fantasies and reverberations and peanut brittle as though nothing were wrong with it.  <sub>[v1 c23 P19](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0019)</sub>

> I am not an old maid from birth, nor did I attain the status... old maidenhood was forced on me... and I resolved that I would be an exceptionally pleasant one.  <sub>[v1 c23 P13](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0013)</sub>
